messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: new package: lavaan.survey
parts:
Dear all,

I'm happy to announce that a new package (lavaan.survey) has been submitted to CRAN. The package was developed by Daniel Oberski, and is a wrapper around the packages lavaan and survey. As a result, all the features of the survey package (clustering, stratification, sampling weights, and finite population corrections) are now available to your SEM analysis in lavaan:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lavaan.survey/

See the documentation for the 'lavaan.survey() function for an example.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: new package: lavaan.survey
parts:
On 10/28/2012 02:21 PM, ya wrote:
> This is a great news. Now I guess lavaan is ready for the multilevel data.

No it isn't. lavaan.survey uses the so-called 'aggregated' approach, not
the 'disaggregated' approach, which corresponds to multilevel modeling.

For more information, see:

Satorra, A., and Muthen, B. (1995). Complex sample data in
structural equation modeling. Sociological methodology, 25, 267-316.

Yves.

messages.author: 949f9be37ba0e6cd
messages.subject: Re: new package: lavaan.survey
parts:
Hi 

Allow me to add a slight nuance: multilevel data, in the sense of clustered data/dependent observations: yes. Multilevel models, in the sense of random effects, no.

You can take into account clustering, stratification, sampling weights, and finite population correction.

Best, Daniel
